in_text_mentions: the exact location of these anatomical points, the adjacent sections were reviewed before establishing the final measurement. Based on the measurements |AB| and |AC|, the taurodontic index (TI) was calculated using the formula TI = (|AB|/|AC|) × 100 [6,19,20] (Figure 1). Taurodontism was considered present when a tooth had a TI > 20 and a |BD| distance > 2.5 mm. According to the TI value, the teeth were classified as hypotaurodontism (20 ≤ TI < 30), mesotaurodontism (30 ≤ TI < 40), and hypertaurodontism (40 ≤ TI < 75) [8,20]. The morphological classification is shown schematically in Figure 2.

in_text_mentions: With regard to associated dental anomalies, taurodontism occurred as an isolated finding in 62 patients (80.5%). Root dilaceration was the most frequently observed associated anomaly (10.4%; n = 8), followed by hypodontia (5.2%; n = 4). Pyramidal molar morphology was identified in 2.6% (n = 2) of patients (Figure 2), whereas pulp stones were detected in 1.3% (n = 1). Chronologically delayed eruption and taurodontism on the first molars (Figure 2) were detected. In addition, profile radiography of the patient's skull showed skeletal class II (Figure 3).
